styleWhy: The product is a desktop app, so the film is told on its own screens: a Mac desktop, its real windows, clicked and typed into.
lookWhy: Shotloop's mood is calm, practical confidence — a maker's tool, not a hype product — and paper's warm off-white ground with heavy black type is the product's own site (#f1f1ee paper, #0a0a0a ink), with its lime accent carrying the end card.

copy.idea: Shotloop is a free, open-source macOS app that turns one sentence into a short video made of shots: the AI writes the copy, the storyboard and each shot's code, and when one shot is wrong you fix that shot in plain words — only it renders again.
copy.hook: One shot is wrong, and the whole film renders again.
copy.body:
The problem, in the maker's own words: the explainers on oliverz.dev were made with a pipeline that rendered the whole film for every check. Feedback was almost always about one shot — the subject too small, hidden behind a caption, nothing moving — but each check still cost a full render: about 8 minutes as a draft, about an hour final, most of it re-rendering shots that had not changed.

Shotloop answers that with shots. You start with one sentence on Home; 2D or 3D, the length, the style and the theme can stay on Auto, and the AI picks how to show it from your idea.

Before anything renders you get the plan: the hook, the script and sourced facts, and the shots with what each one shows — all editable. Then the AI builds every shot.

In the Studio you look at a shot and say what is wrong in plain words, such as "it's too still: add some motion". The AI offers a few ways to change that shot, you pick one, and it changes the shot and shows you a before and after. A fix re-renders that shot only, not the whole film.

Export joins the shots, adds the voice-over, subtitles and music, designs a cover and writes the post for each platform, into a folder of its own.

The one thing to remember: fix one shot, not the whole film. Free and open source, for macOS.

facts.text: Shotloop's tagline: "Short videos with AI. Fix one shot, not the whole film."
facts.source: Shotloop README and product page, https://oliverz.dev/products/shotloop

facts.text: Feedback was nearly always about one shot, but each check meant rendering the whole 48 s: ~8 min as a draft, ~1 h final; most of that time re-rendered shots that had not changed.
A film is a list of shots; each shot is cached by a hash of its inputs, so a fix re-renders one shot in seconds, and Export only joins clips.
On Home you start with one sentence: 2D or 3D, the length, the style and the theme can stay on Auto; the AI picks 2D or 3D, and how to show it, from your idea.
Copy & storyboard: the hook, the script and sourced facts, and the shots with what each one shows, all editable before anything renders.
Tell the shot assistant what's wrong and it offers two to four concrete ways to change the shot; you pick one and it changes that shot and shows a before/after.
Export joins the shots, lays the voice-over with its subtitles and the music under them, designs a cover and writes the post for each platform, into a folder of its own.
Shotloop is out, free, and open source under the Apache 2.0 license; this version runs on Macs with Apple silicon.

shots.title: Title card
shots.show: Title card (screens.js titleCard()) on the paper ground, standing alone with no chapter label and no headline beside it: the real logo repo/logo.png at the left, as tall as the capitals of the name, and just after it SHOTLOOP in the site's Archivo black; under them, on the same left edge, a hairline ink rule and, small and secondary in mono, the product line "Short videos with AI — macOS". The lockup sits centred in the frame and fills most of its width; a faint lime field (#d4ff3a) breathes behind the logo only.
shots.motion: Logo and name rise together out of their mask in a 0.45 s ease-out; the rule draws left to right over 0.4 s, staggered 80 ms; the small mono line fades up last. The whole lockup drifts up about 1% over the beat so nothing is frozen. No bounce.
shots.sound: a soft low swell as the lockup lands, one quiet click as the rule finishes drawing

shots.title: 01 — The problem
shots.show: Chapter device: mono label "01 — THE PROBLEM" over a hairline rule, SHOTLOOP small at the right; this label style, place and colour hold for every chapter of the film. Under the headline, the row device (screens.js row): seven big shot tiles in one row across the frame, each a wireframe of a film shot with a chip under it; tile 4 is marked wrong with a thin ink outline and a small mono chip "TOO STILL". Then every one of the seven tiles dims and runs a progress sweep — all seven render again — with a small mono label under the row carrying the words the caption no longer says: "whole film re-renders · ~8 min draft". The counter device sits in the footer over a rule: "7 / 7" in red with the small label "shots render again". The row is the only picture, keeps its own proportions and fills the frame's middle band.
shots.motion: Headline rises line by line (second line muted), 80 ms apart; the seven tiles rise in a wave left to right, 60 ms apart; the outline snaps onto tile 4; then the sweep runs across all seven in turn and the counter rolls 0 → 7 and turns red. The beat ends on an ink wipe panel starting to cross the frame.
shots.sound: a low tick per tile as the row lands, a dull thud as the wrong shot is marked, a rising whirr under the seven sweeps
shots.source: Shotloop, docs/PRD.md: feedback was nearly always about one shot, but each check rendered the whole film (~8 min draft, ~1 h final)

shots.title: 02 — One sentence
actions: click the idea field "— what is the video about?"
type How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
shots.show: Chapter label "02 — ONE SENTENCE" over its rule, headline beside it, and the one desktop of the film (screens.js desktop(): wallpaper, menu bar, Dock) filling most of the frame with the Shotloop window on it, showing repo/pictures/09-home.jpg — Home, "Let's make a short 2D explainer" and the idea field. Dive to the action: the desktop's camera moves in and centres the idea field and the row of chips under it (Auto · 2D · 3D · 9:16 · 16:9 · Auto length · Style · Theme), big enough to read at phone size — those chips carry in the picture what the caption no longer spells out. Cursor action: the large pointer glides on a curve into the field and clicks, a soft ring letting go; the words are typed in key by key at the field's own size and colour with a blinking caret; then the pointer moves down and clicks the 16:9 chip, which takes its selected state.
shots.motion: Headline rises line by line; the desktop's camera glides in over 1.2 s and keeps pushing about 4% for the rest of the beat; the pointer travels on a smooth curve, presses, releases a ring; typing runs at an even pace with a caret blinking; the chip's state changes in a 0.2 s blend. Ends on the wipe.
shots.sound: a soft click on each press, light key taps under the typing, a small confirm tick when the chip selects
shots.source: Shotloop README, Product tour — Home: one sentence; 2D or 3D, the length, the style and the theme can stay on Auto

shots.title: 03 — The plan, before anything renders
actions: click the Frame field of shot 2 "Sun to Earth: 149.6 million km = 1 AU"
type a gold ruler draws from the Sun to Earth
shots.show: Chapter label "03 — THE PLAN" over its rule; three short mono chips under the headline carrying what the caption drops: COPY · STORYBOARD · SOURCES, with a small mono line under them, "before anything renders". The same desktop in the same box, now showing repo/pictures/01-plan.jpg — Copy & storyboard, with the hook, the script, facts and sources on the left and the seven numbered shots on the right. Dive to the action: the camera comes in on the storyboard column so shot 2's card and its Frame field are the biggest, most readable thing in the frame. Cursor action: the pointer glides into shot 2's Frame field and clicks; the words are typed into it in the screen's own font and size, caret blinking; then the pointer rises to "Make the video" at the top right and clicks it, the button taking its pressed state.
shots.motion: Headline rises, then the three chips light one after another, 90 ms apart; camera glides in and keeps pushing 4%; pointer curves to the field, clicks, words type in; pointer curves up to the button and presses. Ends on the wipe.
shots.sound: chip ticks as the three light, key taps under the typing, a firm click on Make the video
shots.source: Shotloop README, Product tour — Copy & storyboard: hook, script and sourced facts, all editable before anything renders

shots.title: 04 — Fix one shot
actions: click It's too still: add some motion
shots.show: Chapter label "04 — FIX ONE SHOT" over its rule. The same desktop in the same box, showing repo/pictures/06-studio.jpg — the Studio: the shot on its dark stage, the filmstrip of seven shots under it, the AI assistant on the left saying it edits 01-hook only. Dive to the action: the camera comes in on the assistant column so its plain-words suggestions are readable at phone size — the screen's own lines ("The text is too small", "It's too still: add some motion") carry in the picture what the caption no longer says. Cursor action: the pointer glides to the suggestion "It's too still: add some motion" and clicks it. Cut (the two screens do not line up) to repo/pictures/03-agent.jpg: the assistant's answer with the Before / After divider and the green "All checks pass". One quiet mark only: a thin ink outline hugging the Before/After card, with a small neutral mono chip "BEFORE / AFTER", drawn on the screen's picture so it moves with the camera. Counter in the footer over a rule: "1 / 7" with the small label "shots render again", the 7 / 7 of chapter 01 struck through beside it.
shots.motion: Headline rises line by line; camera glides in over 1 s and keeps pushing 4%; the pointer curves to the suggestion and presses with a ring; cut to the answer screen, whose outline draws round the before/after card in 0.3 s; the counter rolls 7 → 1 and the old number is struck through. Ends on the wipe.
shots.sound: a click on the suggestion, a short whoosh on the cut, a soft tick as the outline closes, a light chime as the counter lands on 1
shots.source: Shotloop 0.12.1 release notes: the assistant offers two to four ways to change the shot, then changes that shot and shows a before/after

shots.title: 05 — Export
shots.show: Chapter label "05 — EXPORT" over its rule. The same desktop in the same box, showing repo/pictures/05-hero.jpg — the Studio with its finished filmstrip and the dark Export button at the top right. Dive to the action: the camera comes in on that corner. Cursor action: the pointer glides to "Export" and presses it; the screen changes to repo/pictures/08-export.jpg — the Export dialog, the AI-designed cover on the left and Video, Cover and Publish copy on the right — and the camera settles so the aspect row and those lines are readable. The pointer then glides to "Horizontal 16:9" and clicks; the checkbox takes its ticked state, the rest of the screen holding still. Small mono chips along the footer rule carry what the caption drops: VOICE-OVER · SUBTITLES · MUSIC · COVER · POSTS, lighting one by one, and a thin ink outline draws round the "Publish copy" line with the chip "WRITTEN FOR YOU".
shots.motion: Headline rises; camera glides in on the Export corner, the screen changes, the camera settles and keeps pushing 4%; the footer chips light 90 ms apart; the pointer curves to the checkbox and presses, the tick blending in over 0.2 s; the outline draws round Publish copy. Ends on the wipe.
shots.sound: a firm click on Export, a short whoosh as the dialog comes up, chip ticks along the footer, a small tick as the box checks
shots.source: Shotloop README: Export joins the shots, lays the voice-over with its subtitles and the music under them, designs a cover and writes the post for each platform

shots.title: End card
shots.show: End card (screens.js endCard()): a full field of the brand lime #d4ff3a, standing alone with no chapter label. Centred as one lockup on a single left edge: the real logo repo/logo.png as tall as the capitals, then SHOTLOOP huge in black Archivo; under a hairline black rule, the line to remember "Fix one shot." and, smaller and secondary on the same edge, "Free and open source · macOS, Apple silicon · oliverz.dev/products/shotloop".
shots.motion: The lime field wipes in from the previous shot's ink panel; the logo and name rise out of their mask in 0.45 s, the rule draws left to right, the line and the address rise 80 ms apart; the whole lockup drifts up about 1% to the last frame.
shots.sound: a warm low swell on the field, a last soft click as the rule lands
shots.source: https://oliverz.dev/products/shotloop — free, open source (Apache 2.0), macOS on Apple silicon
